items.title: Ray Ricker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 27, 2022
items.q: Well those first two were done with the Rochester Philharmonic, which is not an Eastman thing, but it’s an organization in its own right.

ctx.x: When he did his first “Friends and Love” and I think it was followed by “Together,” what was — was there an attitude discernable from the Eastman Philharmonic about this young man who is coming in with these hand-written parts and bringing in an electric bass guitar and that kind of thing? How did that fly?

Well those first two were done with the Rochester Philharmonic, which is not an Eastman thing, but it’s an organization in its own right. Okay? But right, they were older, more experienced players and you know it’s like anything you’re going to have people that raise their nose and think it’s, you know, beneath them. And then you’re going to have the other people that are in favor of it you know. And it couldn’t have been that much push-back because they were happy to take the money, okay? Happy to play the gig.…
It’s rather stunning, the state of jazz education how it just sort of exploded over the years and now it’s an integral part of almost any music school across the country.
